starship-block3-ship.name: Starship ship, Block 3
notes: Tier: Ship 39, a Block 3 ship, flew on Flight 12 on 2026-05-22 with six Raptors, one of which shut down early; it splashed down in the Indian Ocean as planned (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship_flight_test_12, retrieved 2026-11-19).
Header tanks are not modelled: all 1,600 t sits in the two main tanks.
SpaceX publishes no geometry for the ship. Positions and inertia are derived numbers whose notes state each assumption.
Minimum throttle and gimbal range are not published for Raptor 3 or Raptor Vacuum 3, so they are absent (unknown), not invented.

source.note: No SpaceX figure for Block 3. This page gives 85 t for Block 2 (marked as needing a better source) and about 100 t for Block 1 (Musk, 2021). A 2026 blog estimates 75 t for the Block 3 ship (https://easytool-me.pages.dev/blog/spacex-starship-v3-guide.html, retrieved 2026-11-17). Includes the six engines.

A uniform shell over the 52.1 m ship height puts the centre of mass at 52.1 / 2 = 26.05 m. 52.1 m is this page's Block 2 height; Block 3 is not given. Engines, thrust structure and flaps sit aft, so the range runs down to 10 m (assumption). On the centre line by symmetry.

Thin cylindrical shell of mass 85 t, radius 4.5 m (half the 9 m diameter on this page), length 52.1 m: across m (R^2 / 2 + L^2 / 12) = 20,087,695.83 kg m2, along m R^2 = 1,721,250 kg m2. Range: plus or minus 30% (assumption); products of inertia plus or minus 1% of the across value (assumption: the airframe is near-symmetric).

1,600,000 kg x OF / (1 + OF). 1,600 t is the Block 3 ship's propellant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship, retrieved 2026-11-17). OF = 3.6 (78% oxygen, 22% methane) is this page's figure for the Raptor family; the range uses OF 3.55 and 3.8, other reported figures.
Half the ship's 9 m diameter. The low end allows 50 mm of wall and insulation (assumption).
capacity / (1,141 kg/m3 x pi x 4.5^2); liquid oxygen density 1.141 kg/L from this page. Low: OF 3.55 and propellant 5% denser when subcooled (assumption). High: OF 3.8.

The oxygen tank ends at the thrust structure (this page), so it is the lower main tank, on the centre line. Its height above the ship's aft end is not published: 4.0 m is assumed for the engine bay. The range is what the stack allows: 0 to 52.1 - 17.25 - 12.93 = 21.92 m.
1,600,000 kg / (1 + OF), OF = 3.6 from this page; the range uses OF 3.8 and 3.55. 1,600 t is the Block 3 ship's propellant (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship, retrieved 2026-11-17).
Half the ship's 9 m diameter. The low end allows 50 mm of wall and insulation (assumption).
capacity / (422.8 kg/m3 x pi x 4.5^2); liquid methane 422.8 g/L at -162 C from this page. Low: OF 3.8 and propellant 5% denser when subcooled (assumption). High: OF 3.55.
Directly above the oxygen tank: its aft end plus its length, 4.0 + 17.2506 m. The range follows from the oxygen tank's ranges.

Engine ring radii and gimbal points are not published: placed on the centre line at the top of the assumed 4.0 m engine bay. Range: anywhere inside the 4.5 m body radius, below the oxygen tank's highest possible aft end.
